$comment: NEW-59 (exponentialTalk (h)): THE work screen, the display coding agents drive with computer use, one spec ×4 (TS reference packages/domain-contract/src/work-screen.ts; desktop epilot crate `work_screen` (the gate, the overlay rule) + ui device_settings (the row); iOS ExpCore WorkScreen.swift and Android domain/WorkScreen.kt mirror `copy` and `options` only). SETTING: per device, `launch_defaults.computerUseDisplayId` = the stable `id` of the picked display (absent or null = Auto; #FEED-161: an id, never the OS order, so a hot-plug or a reorder never moves the work screen to another monitor; the number key of #1295 is gone, no legacy). A client save without the key keeps the stored one and an explicit null clears it to Auto; the stored row then carries NO key, and the device reads the row's launch_defaults as a full snapshot, so a missing `computerUseDisplayId` there IS Auto (#1295 review: a remote Auto must reach the device). UPGRADE (#FEED-161): a device whose local pick has never been pushed (no `computerUseDisplayId` sync yet) pushes it on its first converge instead of taking the row's missing key as Auto. DISPLAYS: the device reports its displays in its doctor (`doctor.displays`, register + heartbeat): `[{id, number, width, height, primary}]` in the OS's order (number = 1-based position, for the label only), width and height in PHYSICAL pixels (a Retina display reports its native pixels, never points); absent = not reported (an older build, the CLI daemon without a display). ID per OS (stable across reconnects and reorders, at most 128 characters, counted as Unicode code points on every side (#FEED-164: Rust `chars()`, zod `[...id].length`, never UTF-16 units)): macOS = the display's UUID (`CGDisplayCreateUUIDFromDisplayID`); Windows = the monitor's device interface path (`EnumDisplayDevicesW` with `EDD_GET_DEVICE_INTERFACE_NAME`); X11 = `edid:` + the first 16 hex of a hash of the output's EDID property, else `output:` + the RandR output name; TWINS (#FEED-164, `idCases`): displays sharing one id (twin monitors without a serial) are told apart by their CONNECTOR, never their order: each twin gets `@` + its connector (macOS the display's `CGDisplayUnitNumber`, Windows the GDI device name `szDevice` without its `\\.\` prefix, X11 the RandR output name), so a reorder never moves a pick to the other twin; only when a twin's connector is unknown or two twins share one do that id's twins fall back to the OS's order (the first keeps the bare id, the next get `#2`, `#3`, …). A display without a twin keeps its bare id (an id stored before #FEED-164 still resolves); a suffixed id is cut so the whole fits 128. UPGRADE (desktop only, `legacyIdCases`): a stored id no reported display carries that is `base` or `base#n` (the order-based twin ids before #FEED-164) names the n-th (bare = the 1st) of the `base@…` twins in the OS's order; the device reads it so and pushes the new id once, until then the other clients list the old one as `copy.notConnected`. SAME MONITOR (#EXP-1919, desktop only, `pickCases`): a display's id changes form when its twin connects or goes (`base` alone, `base@connector` beside a twin); the pick stays on its monitor. Next to the pick the device keeps `seen`, the `base@connector` form of the display it last saw carrying it (local, never on the wire). A stored `base@connector` no display carries names the lone display `base` on that connector; a stored bare `base` no display carries names the display whose id is `seen` when `seen` is that id's own `@` form, and is not connected without it (never another twin); only a pick never seen falls to the UPGRADE rule. On every converge the device rewrites its stored pick to the id that display carries now and pushes it. The hub itself reads only an exact id or the lone display on the stored connector (`hub`): between a hot-plug and the rewrite a pick is at worst not connected, never another monitor. UI: in device settings ×4 (web, the IDE, iOS, Android) the row `copy.row` is a picker row in the computer-use card, directly under the Computer use model row and only while computer use is on (the same group, the same picker row, no new component). Its options = `options(displays, storedId)` (`optionCases`; the value is the display's `id`, null = Auto; the stored value is always the bare id. #FEED-164 `pickerKeys`: a picker keyed by strings (web, the IDE, Android; iOS binds the optional itself) keys Auto as `pickerKeys.auto` and a display as `pickerKeys.display` + its id, so no id can ever read as Auto; `pickerKeyCases`): `copy.auto` first, then one per reported display labelled `copy.display` with {number} plus ` · ` + `{width} × {height}`, plus ` · ` + `copy.primary` for the primary; a stored id the device no longer reports stays pickable at the end labelled `copy.notConnected`. The row's value reads the picked option's label. GATE (desktop only; the `computer` hub enforces it, never the prompt; `gateCases`): `workDisplays(state)` = the 0-based indexes agents may drive: the picked display when it is connected; a picked display that is NOT connected = none (#1295 review: a person who picked a screen keeps agents off the others, so a hot-unplug never widens the set); Auto = every display WITHOUT a fullscreen app, in order. `state` = {count, picked (the 1-based number of the display whose id is stored, 0 when that id is not connected, null = Auto), fullscreen (0-based indexes holding a fullscreen window), active (0-based index of the focused window's display or null), activeFullscreen (the focused window is fullscreen), windowsRead (false = the OS window list could not be read; absent = true)}. A display is a GAMING display when it holds a fullscreen app and is not a work display. NUMBERING: refusals speak the tools' own 0-based display INDEX (`list_windows` / `screenshot`), {display} and {work} (the work indexes joined with `, `); only `pickedGone` names the person's 1-based setting ({picked}). `gate(state, call)` answers `allow` or the refusal `wrong_display` with one of `copy.refusals`, checked in this order (`wait` is always allowed): a picked display that is gone = `pickedGone`; no work display at all = `noWorkScreen`; an input tool or `list_windows` while the window list could not be read = `noWindowList` (fail closed: no focus or fullscreen reading means no input); `screenshot` with a `display` outside the work displays = `notWorkScreen`; `activate_window` of an id `list_windows` does not list or whose centre lies on no display (`windowDisplay` null) = `unknownWindow` ({id}), on a non-work display = `windowElsewhere`; every INPUT tool (`inputTools`) while the focused window is fullscreen on a gaming display = `gaming` (the person is in it, and a foreground action would take their pointer and keyboard); the KEYBOARD tools (`keyTools`: `type`, `key` and the clipboard's `paste_text` and `copy_selection`, which press their shortcut into the focused window) while the focused window sits on a non-work display = `keysElsewhere`. In AUTO without a window list every tool but `wait` is refused with `noWindowList` (#FEED-161: no fullscreen reading, so no display is known to be free; a connected PICK still allows `screenshot`). A window's display = the display its rect overlaps MOST (ties: the lower index; #FEED-161, never its centre alone). Everything else is allowed; the run's current display is the picked `screenshot` display while it stays a work display, else the primary when it is one, else the first work display (`currentCases`). `list_windows` lists only windows whose centre lies on a work display and only the work displays (their indexes unchanged). A refusal is a tool result with isError true, the text `copy.refusals[kind]` and structuredContent {refusal: `wrong_display`, kind, work: [indexes]}. FULLSCREEN (per OS, read at every call): macOS = a layer-0 on-screen window of another app than the Dock/Finder/Window Server whose bounds equal a display's full bounds, or (a notched MacBook places a fullscreen window below the camera housing) whose bounds equal the display less the menu-bar strip at the top and whose own Accessibility `AXFullScreen` is true (without Accessibility that shape counts as not fullscreen, since a zoomed window with the Dock hidden has the same frame); Windows = a visible, non-tool top-level window (never Progman/WorkerW/the shell tray) whose rect covers its monitor's full rect; Linux X11 = a `_NET_CLIENT_LIST` window with `_NET_WM_STATE_FULLSCREEN`, on the display holding its centre. OVERLAY: the voice overlay (push to talk, the wake word, calls) never opens on a display with a fullscreen app: `overlayDisplay(state)` (`overlayCases`; state = {count, pointer (0-based display under the pointer), fullscreen, work}) = the pointer's display without one, else the first work display without one, else the first display without one, else null (the overlay stays hidden; the turn still runs and the reply is still spoken). HOLD (#EXP-1898, desktop only): only a DRIVING tool (`inputTools`, plus `read_clipboard`) takes the person's input for its call (computer-use-banner.json) and queues with the other driving calls; `screenshot`, `list_windows`, `cursor_position` and `wait` never take the hold, never renew it and never queue, so `wait` (always allowed) never locks. BANNER: the computer-use banner (computer-use-banner.json) floats on the run's current display (the work screen), not the primary, with the session's label. AGENT SPACE (#EXP-1514): the stored pick `space.value` (reserved: no display id is ever that bare word; `pickerKeys.space` is its picker key) means agents work in an agent space of their own and never on this device's screen. OPTIONS x4 (`options(displays, stored, spaceOffered)`, absent = false, so `optionCases` replay unchanged; `spaceOptionCases`): while the device offers a space (device-doctor.json: its `agent_space` row is `ok`), Auto reads `copy.auto` + ` · ` + `space.label` and `space.only` follows it; `space.only` also stays while it is the stored pick, never `copy.notConnected`. MEANING: Auto = an agent space when the device offers one, else every display without a fullscreen app; `space.value` = an agent space only (none offered = no computer use); a display = that display only, never a space. PLACE (desktop only; `place(input)`, `placeCases`): the launcher's answer at every launch, `none`, `person` or `space`, from the switch, the session (`computerUse`; `place`, auto unless sessions carry one), the pick (`auto`, `space`, `display`), the offer (`offered`; `no` = a stable reason; `unknown` = an Exponential Desktop that did not answer) and whether the person's screen can be driven. `unknown` is never the person's screen. GATE (`spaceGateCases`): with the pick `space.value` (`state.spaceOnly`) every tool but `wait` is refused `spaceOnly`, checked first; the pick also releases a hold a person run still has. SCREEN MEMORY and the voice overlay read `space.value` as Auto (screen-memory.json).

refusals.noWorkScreen: Every display has a fullscreen app, so there is no work screen right now. Wait, or ask the person to leave fullscreen.
refusals.pickedGone: The work screen picked in Device settings is not connected. Nothing is done until it is back or the setting changes.
refusals.noWindowList: The window list can't be read right now, so nothing is done. Try again.
refusals.notWorkScreen: Display {display} is not a work screen. Agents work on display {work}.
refusals.unknownWindow: Window {id} is not one list_windows names on a work screen. Agents work on display {work}.
refusals.windowElsewhere: That window is on display {display}, not a work screen. Agents work on display {work}.
refusals.gaming: The person is in a fullscreen app on display {display}. Acting now would take their pointer and keyboard; wait until they leave it.
refusals.keysElsewhere: The focused window is on display {display}, not a work screen. Activate a window on display {work} first.
refusals.spaceOnly: This device keeps agents in agent spaces. Nothing is done on its screen.
